d: 00 Start Here: How to Use the SIDE EYE Art Direction Standards
t: If you follow only these, you avoid the worst mistakes. 1. Heather has the final yes. Nothing prints, posts or uploads, and nothing is marked Approved, without her sign-off. AI agents never mark anything Approved. 2. The Scorecard binds the art. No image may show or suggest anything on a feature's Must NOT claim list, or any crime, deal or motive the Scorecard can't prove. 3. One print process per image: RELIEF, COLLAGE, WOOD TYPE, HYBRID or NEWSPRINT. Don't invent a new look. 4. In print, use black plus two inks per image and one pink focus per page. Keep total ink under 240%. Covers and the tabloid may use more inks. 5. QUIET pages get no neon, no collage and no jokes. Serious subjects (deaths, atrocities, real suffering) are always QUIET. 6. No generated lettering, anywhere. Every word is set in type or hand-lettered. Never generate the logo. Place it from the logo pack. 7. Never name an artist, studio, shop or magazine in a prompt. Describe materials and methods only. 8. Never recolor period art pink or neon. An illustration never imitates a period document or sits inside one. Illustrations carry the argument. Period images carry the proof. 9. Every image needs a cleared rights line and a credit line before layout locks. No paid licenses. 10. Real people: generated likenesses of historical figures are allowed. Living people follow the sourced-public-facts-only rule and are never shown doing something we can't prove. 11. Respect the print limits: 7 pt minimum type, 300 dpi at placed size, and nothing essential within 0.5 in of the gutter. 12. When sources disagree, don't pick. Use the source-of-truth order below. If that doesn't settle it, follow what the set says to follow and log the question.

h: 4. How editorial hands off to design
t: Design does not invent or check facts. It works from what editorial hands over. The handoff happens per feature (so art direction can start early) and then for the whole issue (so layout can start). Per feature, before Stage 2 starts on it - Text locked. The feature's text is approved by Heather. Status LOCKED in the file name or header. - Scorecard with the Must NOT claim list. Every rated claim, plus the list of things the piece must never say or imply. The Must NOT list binds the art as much as the text: art never implies a crime, deal or motive that the Scorecard rates below Proven (side-eye-art-direction skill). - Research package accepted. The package from the research process (Fact Ledger, sources doc, rulings, Living Person Register where living people appear), accepted by Heather at the research hand-off gate (R8 in the Research Guidelines Portal plan). - Register and tab. LOUD or QUIET, and which of the issue's three tabs the piece files under. - Word count for the text and each sidebar. For the whole issue, before Stage 4 starts - The full manuscript is LOCKED, including the opening letter, departments, captions written by editorial, cover lines and the issue thesis line. - The fact-check log is closed: zero open items, or each one signed by Heather. - The back-of-issue sources section text exists and matches the fact-check log one to one (Brand Standards hub, "What's in every issue"). - The headline pass is done. What design does when a handoff item is missing Do not start the stage for that piece. Log it in the production tracker as blocked, name the missing item, and work on another piece. Never fill a gap with your own facts, quotes, numbers or dates. New facts found during design Any fact, number, date or quote that design adds (an infographic figure, a caption, a pull quote, a map pin, a cover line) goes back to Fact-check / Research as a change request. It gets a ledger row, a rating and a check before it prints (Research Guidelines Portal plan, section 7.1). Packaging is rated too: cover lines and headlines follow the same scale as the body. ---

t: Stage 0: Issue Brief Purpose. Fix what the issue is, what it costs and when it ships, before anyone designs a page. Inputs (must exist before you start). - The issue's plan in the content calendar (theme, thesis, three tabs, lineup). - A lineup with a status and rough word count for every piece. - A proposed launch (on-sale) date from Heather. - The issue's research tier list (which features run the full research process). Steps. 1. Copy the Issue Brief template (doc 11) into the issue's plan folder. 2. Fill theme, thesis line, audience, volume number and launch date from the calendar and Heather's notes. Use the newest Heather decision where the calendar and the manuscript disagree, and say which you used. 3. Set the page count target. It must be even. Plan 116 to 132 pages (Design System v2 Addendum A). Over 150 pages changes the gutter and the grid, so flag it. 4. List the features with tab, register and word count. Confirm the issue rules: at least one QUIET feature; at least two stories centered on women and two from outside Europe (content calendar, "Rules every volume follows"). 5. Copy in the issue's Must NOT claim list: the combined Must NOT lines from every feature's Scorecard, plus issue-level flags from the calendar. 6. Write the hero idea: one surreal cover idea, and the cover side. The hero alternates sides by volume (Vol. 1 right, Vol. 2 left; Brand Standards hub, "What's in every issue"). Doc 02 says which side each volume takes. 7. List every item KDP cannot print and how it will be redrawn: no gatefolds, inserts, die cuts, perforations or spot inks (Addendum A, sections 1 and 5). 8. Send the brief to Heather with a Handoff Note. Outputs. The approved Issue Brief, filed in the issue's 01 Plan folder (doc 09 sets the name). Who. AD drafts. h: 7. How changes are requested and recorded
t: When you need a Change Request Use the Change Request template (doc 11) for any change after a gate has passed that: - changes the page count, the running order or a piece's page budget; - changes locked text (editorial owns the fix; design never edits locked text); - changes the cover, a cover line or an approved concept; - adds a fact, number, quote or date (it also goes to Fact-check / Research); - swaps an image for one with a different process or rights status; - moves the launch date or a gate date; - spends money or adds a paid service; - needs a color, font, logo use or format not in the Brand Standards hub. Small fixes inside an approved item (a typo in a caption, a crop, a widow, a kerning fix, a reflow within the same pages) need no Change Request. Note them in the build's change notes. The steps 1. Anyone can raise a Change Request. Give it the next number for the issue ( CR-001 , CR-002 and so on). 2. The AD triages it within one working day: what it touches, what it costs in days, which stages must run again. 3. Decide it at the right level: - AD decides: anything inside an approved concept that keeps page count, running order, cover and text the same. - Editorial decides, Heather approves: any change to locked text. - Heather decides: everything else on the list above. 4. Record the decision in the issue's Change Log (the CR list in the issue's plan folder) and in the production tracker. 5. Re-run the checklist for every stage the change touched. Rules - Never apply a change before it is decided, even a "quick" one. - A change that touches a fact always goes through Fact-check / Research. - If Heather's answer is not in writing, it is not decided. ---

A SIDE EYE cover is one surreal picture that argues the issue's thesis. It is built as a COLLAGE in six layers. A photoreal cut-out hero with oversized eyes leans in from one side and breaks the frame. The logo sits in a flat color field at the top with room around it. Four cover lines at most, set in typewriter mono on torn paper strips. The issue title runs down one edge, and the thesis line sits with it. If you remember five rules: 1. One surreal idea per cover, and it must say the issue's thesis. 2. Never put any lettering in generated art. Every word is set in layout, and the logo is a placed file. 3. Four cover lines, maximum. Every line is true on the issue's fact-check log. 4. The hero comes in from the right on odd volumes and from the left on even volumes. 5. Build the wrap on KDP's own template for the final page count. Never guess the spine. Heather has the final yes on every cover. No agent or vendor marks a cover approved. ---

h: 2. Where covers sit in the issue process
t: The cover is made late on purpose. The thesis and the cover lines must be locked first, because the picture has to argue them. Step What must be true before you start Who signs off :- :- :- Thesis locked The issue thesis is final in the Issue Hub Heather Cover lines picked The headline pass is done and Heather picked four lines or fewer Heather Concept One-sentence idea, hero, hero side and joke written down Heather picks A or B Art A and B prompts generated, best result cut out and composited Art director Type and logo Masthead file placed, type set, nothing generated Art director Wrap Interior page count final, KDP template downloaded Production (see 07) Preflight KDP previewer clean, cover checklist passed Production, then Heather The full order of work is in 01 Issue Design Process: From Brief to Print-Ready Files. The detailed approval steps for covers are in section 12 below. ---

Rule 3.1. One surreal idea. Write the idea in one sentence before you make anything. If you need "and" to describe it, it is two ideas. Cut one. Rule 3.2. The picture argues the thesis. A reader who sees only the picture should get the issue's point. Write one line that ties the picture to the thesis. Example from Vol. 1 (The Losers Issue, thesis "History belongs to whoever keeps the files"): a second-place podium in an empty wheat field, an old army truck, and an emu peeking in from the right. The joke: the emu won, and nobody gave it the podium. Rule 3.3. The joke must be true. The cover is held to the same proof standard as the articles. It must not imply a crime, deal or motive that the issue's Scorecard rates below Proven. The Scorecard's "Must NOT claim" list binds the cover art too. Rule 3.4. Everyday things out of place. The surreal idea comes from ordinary objects in the wrong place (a podium in a wheat field, an envelope over a swimming pool). Avoid fantasy scenes, space, glowing magic or anything that looks rendered on a screen. Rule 3.5. Write two concepts. Concept A is the safer read. Concept B is the bolder joke. Heather picks one, or asks for another round. Rule 3.6. Who the hero can be. The hero is an animal or an object with oversized eyes (the emu, the peacock). A historical figure may be the hero as a clear caricature, because generated likenesses of historical figures are allowed. Do not make a living person the cover hero. Living people follow the sourced-public-facts-only rule, and the house rule is never to joke about anyone's looks. (See 13 Open Questions for Heather if a future issue needs a living person on the cover.) ---

Every cover is a COLLAGE (Design System v3: Neon Zine Print). Build it in these six layers, bottom to top. Keep each layer on its own layer or group in the layout file, so any part can be changed without regenerating the rest. Layer What goes in it How it is made Vol. 1 example :- :- :- :- 1. Ground Cream or kraft paper, scraps of old print at the edges Midjourney background or scanned paper Aged paper, newsprint scraps at the bottom edge 2. Scene One photoreal scene colored in flat silkscreen fields Midjourney background Outback wheat field, flat blue sky, vintage truck, second-place podium 3. Color fields Flat neon blocks with hard edges; the top block holds the masthead Midjourney blocks out the shape; you lay a flat vector fill in the house CMYK build over it Flat pink block across the top third 4. Marks A loose painted neon brush border, a thin wobbly black ink frame, scanned handwritten margin notes Midjourney for the border and frame; real scanned handwriting for notes Pink brush border and black ink frame round the cover; handwriting down the left edge 5. Hero A photoreal cut-out subject with exaggerated, oversized eyes, breaking the frame from one side Midjourney hero on a white ground, cut out in Photoshop The emu, peeking in from the right, eyes swiveled at the reader 6. Cover lines Short lines set in type on torn paper strips Set in layout, printed or photographed on torn paper, pasted on "Australia vs. 20,000 Emus" on a torn strip in typewriter mono (approved emu draft) Rules for the layers: - Rule 4.1. Never mix RELIEF and COLLAGE in the cover frame. The HYBRID recipe is for feature openers, not covers. - Rule 4.2. Covers may use more than black plus two inks. Use the house inks only (Toner Black, Side Eye Pink, Pale Cyan, Neon Orange, Acid Yellow, Tab Red, Tab Blue, Deep Navy, Peach for period skin, Warm Cream, Kraft). Builds are in the Brand Standards hub, section Color. - Rule 4.3. Set every flat color field as a vector fill in its CMYK build (for example Side Eye Pink C0 M72 Y10 K0). Never rely on the pink that Midjourney painted. On Vol. 1 the masthead field came from the generated art and printed salmon, not Side Eye Pink. - Rule 4.4. Keep total ink under 240% everywhere, including under the hero and in dark fields. Rich black for big fields is C50 M40 Y40 K100 (230%). - Rule 4.5. Paper and texture go in the art around the logo, never on the logo. - Rule 4.6. Beyond the pink masthead field and pink brush border that the v3 template uses

Rule 5.1. Breaks the frame. The hero crosses the black ink frame and the brush border and runs off the trim on its side. On Vol. 1 the emu crosses the frame, overlaps the masthead field, and runs off the right edge and the bottom. Rule 5.2. Oversized eyes, looking at the reader. The eyes are exaggerated and round, and they swivel toward the reader in a side-eye. The eyes are the first thing a shopper sees after the logo. Rule 5.3. Side alternates by volume. Odd volumes: the hero leans in from the right. Even volumes: from the left. The covers then face each other on a shelf. Volume Issue (as planned November 24, 2026) Hero enters from :- :- :- Vol. 1 The Losers Issue Right Vol. 2 The Money Is Fake Issue Left Vol. 3 The Mating Issue Right Vol. 4 The Poison Issue Left The issues were renumbered on November 24, 2026 (Money Is Fake moved ahead of Mating). Always go by the volume number in the Issue Hub, never by an older plan. Design System v2 shows a peacock entering from the left as "Vol. 2"; that peacock now belongs to Vol. 3, so it enters from the right. Rule 5.4. Keep the face safe. The hero's eyes and face stay at least 0.25 in inside the trim and 0.375 in from the spine fold. Only the body, feathers, fur or the edge of an object may run off the page. Rule 5.5. Stay out of the logo's clear space. The hero may overlap the masthead's color field. It never enters the logo's clear space (section 6). Rule 5.6. Cover lines never cross the eyes or face. A strip may overlap a neck, a wing or a background. Rule 5.7. One hero. No second animal, no crowd. Generate props for the hero separately and composite them if Midjourney drifts. Rule 5.8. Resolution. The hero cut-out must be 300 dpi at placed size. Nothing below 200 dpi gets placed. Upscale before cutting out (Vol. 1 art used a 4x upscale), then sharpen after scaling. ---

The logo rules live in the Brand Standards hub, section Logo. Read it before you place the masthead. What a cover designer needs at hand: Rule 6.1. Place the file. Never rebuild it. The masthead is the logo pack's horizontal lockup with tagline (file name pattern SIDE-EYE_horizontal-tagline_<color ), print CMYK PDF. Never retype SIDE EYE or HISTORY, ALLEGEDLY. in Anton or any font, and never ask Midjourney for the logo or the words. Vol. 1 was set before the logo pack existed and used typed Anton letters; do not copy that. Rule 6.2. Check the version. Use the newest logo pack on the Brand Standards hub (version 1.1 as of November 24, 2026). Work already started may finish on the old version within 30 days. Rule 6.3. Position. Put the masthead in the top color field, aligned to the outside and top live-area edges, with air around it. It is the highest element on the cover except an optional banner line (see the open question on banners in section 14). Rule 6.4. Clear space. On a cover, leave the height of the eye (about 1.75X) on every side, where X is the width of the pink iris in the file you placed. The bare minimum is 1X. Measure from the eye's points, the letter edges and the tagline's comma. Nothing enters the clear space: no hero, no strip, no brush stroke, no busy picture detail. Rule 6.5. Size. Make the masthead as wide as the top field allows after clear space. Never place the tagline lockup smaller than 60 mm wide (the print minimum). If you use the positive version (black and pink) on cream, it must be at least 132 mm wide, because the pink tagline is hard to read on light grounds. Rule 6.6. Which version on which field. Pick the file by the field color. Never edit the file's colors. Top field color Logo version Never :- :- :- Side Eye Pink Mono-black A pink iris on pink Tab Red Mono-black Pink Tab Blue Mono-white Pink, black Neon Orange, Acid Yellow, Pale Cyan, Kraft Mono-black Pink Toner Black or Deep Navy Reverse (cream and pink) Positive Warm Cream Positive (black and pink), 132 mm wide or more Reverse Busy photo or art The plate file (reverse on a black box) Any version straight on the image Rule 6.7. The iris always glances right. Never flip, rotate, stretch, outline, shadow, glow or texture the logo. ---

h: 7. Tagline, issue title and thesis line
t: Rule 7.1. Tagline. The tagline is "HISTORY, ALLEGEDLY." It is part of the masthead lockup file. Do not set it again anywhere on the front. The old tagline "History, with receipts." is retired; never use it. Rule 7.2. Issue title. Copy the issue title exactly as written in the Issue Hub (for example THE MONEY IS FAKE ISSUE). Check that it matches the KDP listing title letter for letter, apostrophes included. Vol. 1 prints "THE LOSERS ISSUE" on the cover and is listed on Amazon as "The Loser's Issue"; do not repeat that mismatch. Rule 7.3. Issue title down one edge. Set the issue title vertically down the edge opposite the hero, in Druk Condensed (Anton fallback), all caps. Read it top to bottom. (Design System v3 and v2; Vol. 1 printed it as a small horizontal label instead. See the open question in section 14.) Rule 7.4. Thesis line on every cover. Every cover carries the issue thesis in one line, set in the body serif italic (Tiempos Text Italic, Source Serif Italic fallback), directly with the issue title. Copy it word for word from the Issue Hub. Vol. 1 printed without its thesis line; that was a miss. Vol. Issue title Thesis line (from the Issue Hub or plan) :- :- :- 1 The Losers Issue History belongs to whoever keeps the files. 2 The Money Is Fake Issue Money is a promise. Someone always enforces it. (default in the Issue Hub until Heather says otherwise) 3 The Mating Issue Who gets to choose? Rule 7.5. Type on the cover is 7 pt or larger, and every word is set in type or real scanned hand lettering. No "handwriting" fonts. ---

Rule 8.1. Four at most. The front carries four cover lines or fewer. A "Plus:" kicker or a banner line counts as one of the four. Past plans broke this every time: Addendum A planned six blurbs plus a kicker for Vol. 1, the printed Vol. 1 front has five lines, and the Mating Issue headline pass lists five lines plus a "Plus" line. Heather picks which four. Rule 8.2. Lines come after the thesis. Write cover lines only after the thesis is locked. They come from the issue's headline pass. Rule 8.3. Short. Keep each line to about 8 words and 40 characters. (The longest Vol. 1 line, RUPERT MURDOCH'S DAD AND THE EMU WAR, is 35 characters.) A line that needs two sentences is a deck, not a cover line. Rule 8.4. Typewriter mono on torn strips. Set each line in typewriter mono (Courier Prime is the free stand-in) on a torn paper strip. Print or photograph the strip so the torn edge, paper grain and shadow are real, then paste it on in layout. Never generate the strip's words. Rule 8.5. Placement. Put strips on the side opposite the hero, at angles of a few degrees, never across the hero's eyes or face, never in the logo's clear space, and at least 0.25 in inside the trim (0.375 in from the spine fold). Rule 8.6. True and in voice. Every line is a bold, arguable claim backed by the piece's own text and logged in the fact-check log. No overstatement (the first Mating draft said Nettie Stevens "found the sex chromosomes," which overstates her work). No lines that announce the research ("We Read the Footnotes"). No "receipts" as a metaphor, no "It's not X, it's Y" lines, and no promises of things KDP can't print (perforations, flaps, inside covers, fold-outs, scratch-and-sniff). Rule 8.7. Case. Use the wording and capitalization Heather approved in the headline pass. Do not restyle them on the cover. ---

Rule 9.1. Volume number. Volumes are numbered in release order. Take the number from the Issue Hub on the day you build the cover. Write it as VOL. N (Vol. 1 spine: "VOL. 1"). Rule 9.2. Where it goes. Put the volume number on the spine when the spine carries text (section 10) and in the back-cover identity line (section 11). The front has no agreed place for it yet; see Gaps in the notes and 13 Open Questions for Heather. Rule 9.3. Cover date. If a cover date is used, copy it from the Issue Hub (for example Feb/Mar 2027 for Vol. 3). Never guess one from the content calendar, which was written before the renumbering. Rule 9.4. No price on the cover. Amazon sets and shows the price. Vol. 1 printed no price. Do not add one unless Heather asks. ---

The spine width comes from the final interior page count. Premium color on white paper: page count × 0.002347 in. Rule 10.1. KDP's text limit. KDP allows spine text only on books with more than 79 pages. Under that, the spine is a solid color with no text at all, not even a number. Rule 10.2. Spine margins. Keep at least 0.0625 in between spine text and each fold. Nothing on the spine may need to line up exactly with a fold, because the fold can drift 0.0625 in either way. Rule 10.3. Text size. Spine text is 7 pt or larger. Take the room for text as the spine width minus 0.125 in. If that room is under about 0.1 in, 7 pt caps won't fit cleanly; leave the spine without text. Interior pages Spine width (in) Room for text (in) Spine text? :- :- :- :- Under 80 under 0.188 none No (KDP) 80 0.188 0.063 Allowed by KDP, too narrow for 7 pt; no text 96 0.225 0.100 Just fits 7 pt caps 112 0.263 0.138 Yes 120 0.282 0.157 Yes 132 0.310 0.185 Yes The planned range for an issue is 116 to 132 pages. Rule 10.4. What the spine says. Until Heather decides (open question, section 14), follow the printed Vol. 1 spine: SIDE EYE · VOL. N · THE <TITLE ISSUE in mono caps, cream on a Toner Black field, reading top to bottom, centered on the spine. Never place the logo lockup on a spine this narrow; it falls under its minimum size. Rule 10.5. Color across the fold. Run the front and back backgrounds at least 0.0625 in past each fold into the spine, or pick a spine color that matches the neighboring cover edge, so fold drift never shows a sliver of the wrong color. ---

The back cover is one of the "money pages": everyone reads it, including people who never open the issue. It must read in under 15 seconds, make one point, and have no text block over 120 words. Rule 11.1. Concept. Until Heather decides (open question, section 14), the back cover is the full-page parody ad planned for that volume in Front and Back Matter, Vols 1-3 (The Money Pages): Vol. 2, The First Bank of Yap; Vol. 3, The Train. Vol. 1 printed a toy-ad parody ("TIRED OF WINNING? CALL THE LOSERS SQUAD!") instead of the planned catalog ad. Design System v3's recipe for the back cover is a RELIEF colorway sheet (one motif repeated in every ink combination); use a colorway sheet only if Heather picks it. Rule 11.2. Art on the back. Build the ad's art in one of the five processes (most often RELIEF or WOOD TYPE), with no generated lettering. Historical figures may appear as generated caricature or toy-style likenesses (Vol. 1 did this with Napoleon, Hatshepsut and Hannibal). Living people may not appear in a way that suggests they did something the issue can't prove. Rule 11.3. Identity line. Set one small mono line near the bottom: SIDE EYE Vol. N · The <Title Issue · History, allegedly. (Vol. 1 did this.) Copy the title exactly as on the front. Rule 11.4. Elevator pitch. Brand Identity: Name, Tagline and Pitch says the pitch belongs on the back cover: "You were right to suspect the story you were told was bullshit. The good news is the truth is more interesting." Vol. 1 left it off. Include it unless Heather says otherwise (open question, section 14). Rule 11.5. Barcode zone. KDP prints the barcode on the back cover in a white box 2 in wide by 1.2 in tall, in the lower right corner, beside the spine. Keep that zone empty: no text, no faces, no key art. Item Value :- :- Barcode box 2.0 in wide × 1.2 in tall Position Lower right corner of the back cover, next to the spine From the spine fold 0.25 in (Vol. 1 measured 0.26 in) From the bottom trim 0.25 in (Vol. 1 measured 0.27 in) What wins The barcode box on KDP's downloaded template for your page count Vol. 1 drew its own white box in this zone. If you draw one, match the template box exactly and put nothing under its edges. Rule 11.6. Bleed on the back. Run the back cover's background 0.125 in past the top, bottom and outside trim. On Vol. 1 the black field stopped at the trim and the bleed was cream, so any cutting drift shows a cream sliver. Rule 11.7. Text safety. All back-cover text sits at least 0.25 i

Export. - CMYK only. Convert every RGB image before export. Vol. 1's cover art image has an old "SIDE EYE" masthead and an old cover-line strip baked into the picture, with new type pasted over them. That locks old words into the art. Keep type on its own live layers. Rule 12.6. File names and handoff. Name and file the cover as 09 File Naming, Folders and Handoff Specs says. The house prompt templates, settings and fixes live in 05 Art and Illustration Direction (with Midjourney Prompt Standards). This section gives the cover pattern only. Add --hd (covers are full-page art). - Background: --ar 17:22 (the trim's shape), --s 250 , the approved emu cover as --sref at --sw 30 . - Hero: --ar 1:2 , no style reference, on a plain white background. - Never name an artist, studio, shop or magazine. 1. Brief. Pull the issue title, volume number, thesis line, cover lines (four or fewer) and cover date from the Issue Hub. Confirm Heather has picked the lines. 2. Concept. Write concept A and concept B: the one-sentence idea, the tie to the thesis, the hero, the hero side (by volume), the top field color and the joke. Check each against the Scorecard's "Must NOT claim" list. 3. Heather picks a concept. No generating at full scale before this. 4. Generate. Run A and B prompts for the background and the hero. Log them. 5. Comp. Build the front at full size: art layers, flat vector fields, placed logo file, set type, torn-strip cover lines. 6. Self-check. Run the cover checklist (section 17). 7. Independent review. A second reviewer (person or agent) checks the comp against this document and the Scorecard. Covers are high-stakes pieces. 8. Heather reviews the front. Show it at full size and at thumbnail size, the way a shopper sees it on Amazon. Heather approves or sends changes. 9. Build the wrap. After the interior page count is final, download the KDP template, build spine and back cover, and export the PDF. 10. Preflight. Run KDP's online previewer and fix every flag. Order a proof copy when Heather has approved one for the issue (neon builds can't be judged on screen). 11. Final yes. Heather approves the final cover PDF before upload. File it in the issue's "to print" folder. ---

The blank flatplan is in 11 Templates. This is the method. Work in this order. 1. Start from the issue's lineup. Take the pieces, tabs, registers and word counts from the issue's Issue Hub and manuscript. Drop anything marked cut. 2. Place the fixed anchors first. Page 1 (title and colophon), 2-3 and 4-5 (front spreads), 6-7 (contents), The Files divider, the map, the timeline, the Out Back opener, the sources section, the classifieds, the last spread and the last interior page. These stay in the same order every issue. 3. Budget pages from words. Use section 2.3. Write the planned page count next to each piece. 4. Start every spread-sized piece on a left (even) page. Every Vol. 3 feature starts on an even page, so its opener reads as a full spread. Use one-page pieces (Still Wrong, the opening letter, section openers, the Field Guide) to fill odd gaps. 5. Set the register of every page. Group QUIET features into runs. When a LOUD page must face a QUIET page, mark the LOUD page's art as the cyan + orange variant. 6. Pair the spreads and check each pair against these limits: - One wood-type plate per spread. - One diagonal headline per spread. - One pink focus per page. - No two navy pages facing each other. - No WOOD TYPE, COLLAGE, stamps or diagonal type on a QUIET page. 7. Count the issue-wide limits: - One full-bleed COLLAGE feature opener per issue (the biggest feature). - One isometric headline per volume. - One typographic pun per LOUD feature at most. - At least one QUIET feature. - One A-to-Z catalog section. 8. Check KDP. No gatefold, insert, flap, perforation or inside-cover content (section 8). Every cut-out has a sacrificial verso. Total pages even and within 116 to 132. 9. Record each page in the flatplan template with these columns: pages, piece, recipe, process, register, tab, inks and paper, image count, headline treatment, word count, status (including OPEN and PENDING). 10. If it runs long, cut in the order the Issue Hub lists. If it runs short, give space back to the longest features first. ---

h: 7. Images and captions on the grid
t: Placing images - Image frames start and end on column edges. Never stop a frame in the middle of a gutter. - The top and bottom edges of a frame sit on baseline grid lines. Snap them; don't eyeball them. - Standard sizes: spot (2 to 4 columns), half page (6 columns, any depth, or 12 columns, half depth), full page in the live area (12 columns, full depth), full bleed (to the bleed edge on top, bottom and outside), spread. - Full-bleed and spread art goes to the bleed edge on the outside, top and bottom. Nothing bleeds into the gutter except art that crosses it on purpose. - Art across the gutter: only where the middle of the image is unimportant, with 0.25 in of duplicated image on each side (Addendum A, doc 07). Faces, headline letters and box-score figures stay 0.5 in clear of the spine. - Body text never sits on art. It sits on a clean paper panel (SE-Obj-Paper-Panel) pasted over the collage. The panel edge sits at least one gutter (0.125 in) outside the text. - Illustrations never sit inside a period image, and period images never sit inside an illustration (hub). Placing captions - Every image gets a caption in SE-Caption, starting with its figure number: FIG. 014. (Vol. 1 guide, still in force). - Put the caption under its image. Its first line sits on the first grid line at least 6 pt below the image's bottom edge. - Caption width: the image width, up to 4 columns. Under a wider image, keep the caption 4 columns wide and align it to the image's outside edge. - Side captions are allowed in the column next to the image. Align the caption's first line with the image's top edge on the grid. - Captions for full-bleed art go on a paper panel inside the live area, or on the facing page keyed by figure number: FIG. 014 (OPPOSITE). Keep them inside the 0.375 in safety. - Cast captions (the playbill cameos) use SE-Caption-Cast: the prop name in caps, then one line. Example: THE BOOT. Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington. - Credit lines use SE-Caption-Credit as the caption's last line when doc 06 says the image needs one on the page. The magazine's single Midjourney credit lives in the front matter and colophon (hub). - QUIET captions: plain facts, no jokes (hub, v3). ---

This comes from the zines (v2, v3). It is one of the strongest signals in the book, so it is rationed. - Where: LOUD feature openers, feature title pages and covers only. Never on QUIET pages. Never on interior body pages. - What may rotate: headlines, section titles on openers, the theme title, rail labels and drop-cap labels. - Axes: horizontal, vertical (90°) and diagonal. One diagonal headline per spread, at most. - What never rotates: body text, decks, captions, sidebars, pull quotes. They stay horizontal and on the grid. - Headlines may overlap images and each other. They never overlap body text, captions or another element's text. - A vertical display headline may read up or down (the Napoleon opener runs NOT SHORT. up the right page). Small rotated labels follow the rail rule: toward the spine. - Rotated and diagonal type stays inside the 0.375 in safety and 0.5 in clear of the gutter. - Across a spread: a headline that spans both pages must break at the gutter, with each side at least 0.5 in from the spine. Split between words, never inside a word. - One typographic pun per LOUD feature (v2), built by hand in layout. - One isometric headline per volume (v2), built in vector. - One headline size per page. Get contrast from scale jumps, not from mixing display faces. The exception is a WOOD TYPE plate, which mixes two wood faces by design. - Use object styles SE-Obj-Rotate-90 and SE-Obj-Rotate-270 for vertical type, so rotations are exact and easy to find. ---

Plates are feature title plates, section dividers, the Box Score, the contents page, Case File posters, promo posters and the back cover (v3). 1. Set every letter in layout from real wood-type digital fonts. Never generated. Midjourney makes only the ink textures, split-fountain fields and woodcut cuts (doc 05). 2. Two faces per plate, at most. Mix a condensed face with a fat or extended one. Free pairs: Ultra with Alfa Slab One, or Rye with Alfa Slab One. Use Rye for one or two words only, because it is very ornamental. 3. All caps. Stacked lines, each a different size, each set to fill the plate's width. The one key word is biggest. On a Box Score, "VS." is biggest. 4. One split fountain per plate, at most. Pink to orange to yellow, or cyan to pink. Apply it in layout by placing the split-fountain field inside the letters. Split fountains appear only on WOOD TYPE plates. 5. Ornaments: heavy rules, stars, pointing hands, arrows and dingbat borders, from the house ornament library. No ornaments with letters in them. 6. Ink texture: add uneven inking, wood grain and edge squash in layout as a texture mask over the type. The type underneath stays live. 7. Stock: cream or kraft. 8. One plate per spread. Never on QUIET pages. 9. Keep live type. When the split fountain or texture needs outlined letters, outline a copy. Keep the live text on a hidden layer named LIVE TYPE so the words can be edited and checked. 10. Ink totals for split fountains are checked in doc 07. ---

Cover lines - Four cover lines at most, short, in typewriter mono on torn paper strips (v3, hub). The words must still be real type. Note the method in your handoff note. - Never generate a cover line. Never use a "typewriter" effect font in place of a real typewriter mono. Hand lettering - Margin notes, arrows, circled words and signatures are real handwriting, scanned. Never a handwriting font (hub, v3). - Scan at 600 dpi grayscale (Addendum A), clean it up, and place it as one ink: K100, or pink if it is the page's one focus. - Signatures are scanned from the hosts' own handwriting. Never draw or fake one. - On QUIET pages, hand lettering is black only and never a joke. ---

h: 15. Naming styles so files hand off cleanly
t: Use the style names in sections 9 and 10 exactly as written, including capitals and hyphens. A vendor or agent who opens your file should find the same names in the same order. - Prefix: every style starts with SE- . Paragraph styles, character styles ( SE-Char- ) and object styles ( SE-Obj- ) each live in their own group. - Groups (InDesign style groups, Affinity style folders): 00 Base , Heads , Body , Boxes , Captions and Rail , Back of Book , Cover , Characters , Objects . - Based on: every paragraph style is based on one of the three base styles. Change the face in a base style and the issue follows. - No local overrides. Before handoff, clear overrides on body text (InDesign: Paragraph Styles panel Clear Overrides; Affinity: Text Styles Reset Formatting). The only allowed overrides are the corrections size (10.8) and manual tracking within -10 to +10 on a single line to fix a widow. - Object styles: SE-Obj-Paper-Panel, SE-Obj-Caption, SE-Obj-Tab, SE-Obj-Rail-Title, SE-Obj-PullQuote, SE-Obj-Proof-Box, SE-Obj-Stamp, SE-Obj-Rotate-90, SE-Obj-Rotate-270, SE-Obj-Image-Grid, SE-Obj-Image-Bleed. - Swatches: name them exactly as the hub names the inks (Toner Black, Side Eye Pink, Pale Cyan and so on). Doc 07 gives the builds. - Master pages (InDesign parent pages, Affinity master pages): A-LOUD (3 × 4 columns), B-QUIET (2 × 6, 15 pt frame grid), C-WideRail (rail + 2 × 5), D-Bleed (no rail, no folio), E-Classifieds (3 × 4, 9 pt frame grid). - Affinity Publisher opens IDML. Style names survive the trip only if they match exactly, so don't rename on import. - HTML and CSS builds (Vol. 1 was built this way): name each class after its style in lower case, for example se-body-loud , se-caption , se-char-figno . CSS has no true baseline grid, so check every page against the grid by eye before export. - Doc 09 owns file names, folders and packaging. Doc 11 holds the template files once they are built. ---

Numerals - Body text: lining figures, proportional (the font's default). - Tables, box scores, contents page numbers, folios: tabular lining figures, numbers right-aligned in columns. - Druk and Anton: lining only. - Fractions: use the font's true fraction glyphs (5 ft 4½ in). Check that every face you use has the symbol. - Ordinals: never superscript. - Dates: American style, April 1, 1821 (hub). - Set numbers as the edited copy gives them. Don't change words to figures or figures to words. Punctuation - Quotes and apostrophes: curly in every face, including the mono and the typewriter mono. Turn on typographer's quotes. Check apostrophes at the start of a word: ’90s , not ‘90s . - Em-dashes: the hub's no em-dash rule covers Heather's copy. The Vol. 1 guide (still in force) bans them in display type and captions. Whether the rule covers print design copy such as the classifieds and money pages is an open question in the hub's Decision log. Until Heather decides: no em-dashes in headlines, decks, captions, pull quotes or any of Heather's copy. In the classifieds and money pages, set the copy exactly as the editor supplies it. Never add or remove a dash yourself. If supplied copy has an em-dash, set the true character (Unicode 2014), spaced as supplied, and flag it in your handoff note. - En dash: ranges only. Hyphen: compound words only. Never two hyphens in place of a dash. - Ellipsis: the single ellipsis character. - Spaces: one space after a full stop. No double spaces anywhere. Search for them before handoff. - Measurements: written out ( 5 ft 7 in ) with no-break spaces. Use true prime marks (′ ″) only if the copy uses symbols. - Brackets: host asides only, as [H.C.] and [E.G.] . - Ampersand: only inside a proper name. - Special letters: the ʻokina in Liliʻuokalani, ʻIolani and Aloha ʻOe is its own character (Unicode 02BB). Never use an apostrophe in its place. Check accented letters (Résumé, Mémorial) in every face. If a glyph is missing, your layout tool will quietly swap in a fallback font. Fix it before export (doc 07). - Case: all caps only in display faces and mono labels. Never set body text in caps. Decks and captions are sentence case. - Non-English text: Latin and French phrases are checked by the fact-checker before setting. Japanese text only when

h: 2. The house look in one paragraph
t: SIDE EYE looks like a 1990s Japanese art zine that ran into an American letterpress show-poster shop: cut-and-paste collage, photocopy grain, neon silkscreen color, stacked wood type, split-fountain ink blends and carved-block illustration. Every image must look printed, pasted or carved by hand, never rendered on a screen. That means flat ink, coarse halftone dots, speckle, slight misregistration, paper you can see, and no glow, chrome, gradient or glossy 3D light. Each picture makes one visual joke with a point, uses black plus two inks, and puts pink on the one thing the reader should see first. The influences are studied for methods and materials only. SIDE EYE never borrows anyone's name, logo, layouts or artwork. ---

h: 5. The joke rule and what pink marks
t: The joke rule. Every RELIEF image (and every HYBRID scene) is one visual joke with a point. The point is the article's argument made visible. The joke comes from objects in the wrong place, at the wrong size, or in the wrong hands. Write the joke in one sentence before you write a prompt: "He thought he was playing a king. He was one piece on someone else's board." If you cannot write that sentence, you do not have a picture yet. The joke must be true on the evidence. See section 13. What pink marks. - Pink goes on the punchline object: the thing the reader should see first (the hat, the coin, the padlock, the one envelope). - Name the pink object in the prompt: "the [object] printed in fluorescent pink." Do not leave pink to chance. - Print keeps one pink focus per page (Brand Standards hub, Decision log). Pink in video can be used freely; that does not carry over to print. - Repeat sets (an icon row, a cameo strip, the AI Dead windows) have so far given each item its own pink prop. Keep doing that, with pink playing the same role in every item of the set, until Heather decides whether a matched set counts as one focus (open question). - The cover and the tabloid poster may carry more pink (masthead field, brush border), but the image still has one pink focus inside it. - The cyan-plus-orange variant has no pink. Its focus is carried by size and placement. ---

Historical figures: generated likenesses are allowed (Heather's decision). Draw them as caricature in a house process (RELIEF, HYBRID, woodcut) or use real period art. Never make a generated likeness look like a photograph or a period record. - Name only documented clothing and objects for the time and role ("First Consul in 1800, dark coat"). - The joke is the action, never the face or body. h: 10. Using a generator other than Midjourney
t: If a vendor uses another image generator, the same standard applies. t: These rules come from the Brand Standards hub (Visual identity AI-generated video, Decision log 2026-11-24). They apply to every promo for the magazine: trailers, social clips, Shorts, animated covers. - Generated footage illustrates an idea. It never stands in for real footage of a real person. - Use it for scenes, objects and moments: a magazine page turning, a letter being written, a newspaper being read, a fire in a fireplace, trees being cleared. - Never show a real person, living or historical, acting on screen in generated footage that a viewer could take for real film of them. - Hands, objects, settings, silhouettes and clearly stylized art are fine. Titles and type are added in the edit. - The Midjourney Prompt Workbook notes Midjourney video clips run 5 seconds (extendable to 21) at 720p. t: Art makes arguments, so art is held to the same proof standard as the text. - Art never implies a claim rated below Proven. Use the research scale: only Documented (script label PROVEN) claims may be drawn as fact. Likely, Contested, Unsupported and Refuted claims are never drawn as if true. - Check each image against the article's Scorecard and its Must NOT claim list. That list binds the art as much as the words. - Watch for implied claims: a hand pulling strings implies control; a leash implies ownership; a figure first in line or larger than the rest implies leadership; a crown implies rule. If the control is only Likely, no strings, leash or hand above him. - Never show a myth happening as if it were true. Apocrypha and Still Wrong art shows the prop, not the myth. - Illustrations carry the argument; period images carry the proof. An illustration never imitates a period print, map, letter, newspaper or document, and never sits inside one. A period image never sits inside an illustration made to look like a document (a fake scroll, ledger page or certificate frame around it). - Generated images are illustrations, never records. Real records come from archives (06). - If no Scorecard came with the article, draw only what the fact-checked text states plainly, and log the gap as an open item. ---

h: 12. When the rights can't be confirmed: replace it
t: Set the row to Blocked and work down this list. Stop at the first one that works. 1. Find the same image at another institution with a clear CC0, public-domain or free-license statement. 2. Find a different public-domain image that proves the same point. 3. Use the record itself: a document, report, court opinion or register entry that is public domain. 4. Draw it in-house: a diagram, chart, map or timeline built in layout. (The Vol. 1 plan called for an in-house X-shaped diffraction diagram in place of a protected photograph.) 5. Illustrate the idea instead of the image: a RELIEF illustration of props, hands or objects, captioned as illustration. Never a re-creation of the protected image. 6. Cut the image and let the text carry the page. Never: buy a license, run it "for now," use a small web copy, trace it, or ask Midjourney to re-create it. ---

5.1 Resolution Use Minimum effective resolution Pixel size needed --- --- --- Full-bleed page 300 ppi 2,588 x 3,375 px (8.625 x 11.25 in) Full-bleed spread across the gutter 300 ppi 5,325 x 3,375 px (17.75 x 11.25 in: two bleed pages plus 0.25 in duplicated on each side of the gutter) Full cover wrap 300 ppi See the table in 2.3 Front cover only 300 ppi 2,588 x 3,375 px Line art, document scans, period engravings 600 ppi, grayscale where possible Placed size x 600 Any image, absolute floor 200 ppi Never place anything lower, at any size Upper limit 600 ppi is enough KDP advises no more than 600 ppi to keep files under 650 MB Effective ppi is the image's pixels divided by the inches it fills on the printed page. A 3,000 px wide image placed 5 in wide is 600 ppi. The same image placed 12 in wide is 250 ppi and fails. Check effective ppi in: - InDesign: Links panel, "Effective PPI" column. - Affinity Publisher: Resource Manager, "DPI" column for placed size. - Any PDF: Acrobat Pro Preflight, "Images with resolution below 300 ppi" check; or the free command-line tool pdfimages -list file.pdf , whose x-ppi and y-ppi columns show effective resolution. 5.2 Getting Midjourney art to print size Midjourney output is usually smaller than a full page at 300 ppi. To get there: 1. Generate with --hd for full-page and spread art (Design System v3). 2. Upscale inside Midjourney first, by hand. Don't automate Midjourney. 3. If still short, upscale with a dedicated image upscaler to the pixel size in 5.1, then check the result at 100% zoom for smeared texture or invented detail. 4. Sharpen after scaling, not before (Addendum A). 5. Convert to CMYK last (section 4.4), then place. 5.3 Halftone textures that survive print The house look depends on coarse halftone, speckle and misregistration. Print can destroy all three if they are too fine. - Make halftone coarse. Dots should be easy to see at 100% zoom at final printed size. Fine dots blur into a flat tint on a digital press. Design System v3 says "coarse halftone dots only." - Apply halftone at final size. If an image with a halftone texture has to grow, re-run the halftone at the new size. Don't enlarge a dotted image; scaling smears the dots. - Don't stack two halftones. A halftone image under a halftone overlay makes moiré (wavy interference patterns). KDP lists overlapping halftones as a known print problem. One halftone layer per area. - Descreen printed sources. Period art scanned from a book, newspaper or magazine al

- Embed every font in both PDFs. A PDF with a missing or partly embedded font fails at KDP. - Use licensed fonts only. The paid faces (Druk Condensed, Tiempos Text, GT America Mono) and the Hamilton wood-type faces have no recorded print license (hub, "Gaps to fill"). Until Heather records a license, print with the free stand-ins that carry the SIL Open Font License: Anton (display), Big Shoulders Display (section heads), Source Serif 4 (body), IBM Plex Mono or Space Mono (captions and labels), Courier Prime (cover lines), Alfa Slab One, Rye or Ultra (wood-type plates). See 04 Grid and Typography for the full stack. - No fallback fonts. If a font lacks a character (an arrow, a star, a fraction, a special letter), the layout tool quietly swaps in a system font. Vol. 1 shipped with DejaVu Sans Mono, Liberation Sans and Liberation Serif in its files this way. Before export, list every font in the PDF (Acrobat: File Properties Fonts; or pdffonts file.pdf ). Any font not on the house list is an error. Fix it by choosing a glyph the house font has, or drawing the symbol as art. - 7 pt minimum for all type, including classifieds, folios, credits and legal lines. - Convert no live body text to outlines. Outlining is fine for display lettering on art, and the logo files are already outlined. ---

h: 14. Packaging the issue for the archive
t: When an issue is released, package it so anyone can rebuild or reprint it without asking. The package lives in the issue's "08 Package" folder, and every name follows 09 File Naming, Folders and Handoff Specs. The package holds: Part Contents --- --- README A plain-text file: issue, version, date, page count, build route and tool version, how to rebuild on a clean machine, ink builds used, conversion setup used, any build changed after the proof, known issues Layout The live layout file (InDesign, Affinity or Scribus document, plus an IDML copy from InDesign), or for the HTML route the HTML, CSS, scripts and manuscript files the build reads Links Every placed image exactly as placed (the finals from 04 Art/09 Finals) Masters The RGB masters and upscales behind each final, for future re-conversion (or a pointer to 04 Art) Fonts Free-license fonts only, with their license files. If a line here ever disagrees with the hub, follow the hub and add the conflict to 13 Open Questions for Heather. Rules for reading a row: 1. Newest Heather decision wins. "Via hub" means the rule sits in the hub, which only Heather approves. 3. "No" means the rule is a team standard, a spec rule or an outside fact (for example, a KDP rule). This follows 01 Issue Design Process: From Brief to Print-Ready Files, section 9. 1. Get Heather's yes in writing. A decision enters this log only after Heather approves it, or after it appears in the hub's Decision log. An agent's or vendor's suggestion is not a decision. 2. Check the hub first. If the decision is about logo, color, type, voice or rights, it belongs in the hub's Decision log. Ask the hub owner to add it there, then copy the line here only if this set relies on it. 3. Add one row in the right section. Use the next free ID (never reuse an ID, even for a row that is later replaced). Fill every column: date (YYYY-MM-DD), the decision as a rule someone can check, the source by title and date, whether it is Heather's own call, and which docs apply it. 4. Mark what it replaces. If it overrides an earlier row, write "Replaced by D-0NN on <date " at the end of the old row's Decision cell. Leave the old row in place. 5. Close the open question. If it answers a question in 13 Open Questions for Heather, move that question to the "Answered" list there with the new decision ID. 6. Fix the docs. Each doc owner updates the docs in "Applied in," bumps their version (whole number if a rule changed, decimal for wording), and notes the decision ID in the change. 7. Tell anyone mid-issue. An issue past Stage 2 may finish on the old rule unless Heather says otherwise (01, section 9). Record which rule the issue used in its Release Note. Only the process owner (the Documentation Specialist for Process and Governance) edits this log. Agents never write "Heather's own call: Yes" without her words or an approved document to point to. ---
